    15  /-!
    16  # Infinite places of a number field
    17  
    18  This file defines the infinite places of a number field.
    19  
    20  ## Main Definitions and Results
    21  
    22  * `NumberField.InfinitePlace`: the type of infinite places of a number field `K`.
    23  * `NumberField.InfinitePlace.mk_eq_iff`: two complex embeddings define the same infinite place iff
    24    they are equal or complex conjugates.
    25  * `NumberField.InfinitePlace.IsReal`: The predicate on infinite places saying
    26    that a place is real, i.e., defined by a real embedding.
    27  * `NumberField.InfinitePlace.IsComplex`: The predicate on infinite places saying
    28    that a place is complex, i.e., defined by a complex embedding that is not real.
    29  * `NumberField.InfinitePlace.mult`: the multiplicity of an infinite place, that is the number of
    30    distinct complex embeddings that define it. So it is equal to `1` if the place is real and `2`
    31    if the place is complex.
    32  * `NumberField.InfinitePlace.prod_eq_abs_norm`: the infinite part of the product formula, that is
    33    for `x ∈ K`, we have `Π_w ‖x‖_w = |norm(x)|` where the product is over the infinite place `w` and
    34    `‖·‖_w` is the normalized absolute value for `w`.
    35  * `NumberField.InfinitePlace.card_add_two_mul_card_eq_rank`: the degree of `K` is equal to the
    36    number of real places plus twice the number of complex places.
    37  * `NumberField.InfinitePlace.denseRange_algebraMap_pi`: the image of `K` by the diagonal embedding
    38    into the product of its infinite completions is dense.
    39  
    40  ## Tags
    41  
    42  number field, infinite places
    43  -/
    44  
    45  @[expose] public section
    46  
    47

    49  
    50  namespace NumberField
    51  
    52  open Fintype Module
    53  
    54  variable (K : Type*) [Field K]
    55  
    56  /-- An infinite place of a number field `K` is a place associated to a complex embedding. -/
    57  def InfinitePlace := { w : AbsoluteValue K ℝ // ∃ φ : K →+* ℂ, place φ = w }
    58  
    59  instance [Nonempty (K →+* ℂ)] : Nonempty (InfinitePlace K) := Set.instNonemptyRange _
    60  
    61  variable {K}
    62  
    63  /-- Return the infinite place defined by a complex embedding `φ`. -/
    64  noncomputable def InfinitePlace.mk (φ : K →+* ℂ) : InfinitePlace K :=
    65    ⟨place φ, ⟨φ, rfl⟩⟩
    66  
    67  /-- A predicate singling out infinite places among the absolute values on a number field `K`. -/
    68  def IsInfinitePlace (w : AbsoluteValue K ℝ) : Prop :=
    69    ∃ φ : K →+* ℂ, place φ = w
    70  
    71  lemma InfinitePlace.isInfinitePlace (v : InfinitePlace K) : IsInfinitePlace v.val := by
    72    simp [IsInfinitePlace, v.prop]
    73  
    74  lemma isInfinitePlace_iff (v : AbsoluteValue K ℝ) :
    75      IsInfinitePlace v ↔ ∃ w : InfinitePlace K, w.val = v :=
    76    ⟨fun H ↦ ⟨⟨v, H⟩, rfl⟩, fun ⟨w, hw⟩ ↦ hw ▸ w.isInfinitePlace⟩
    77  
    78  namespace InfinitePlace
    79  
    80  instance : FunLike (InfinitePlace K) K ℝ where
    81    coe w x := w.1 x
    82    coe_injective _ _ h := Subt

    11  
    12  /-!
    13  # The completion of a number field at an infinite place
    14  
    15  This file contains the completion of a number field at an infinite place. This is ultimately
    16  achieved by applying the `UniformSpace.Completion` functor, however each infinite place induces
    17  its own `UniformSpace` instance on the number field, so the inference system cannot automatically
    18  infer these. A common approach to handle the ambiguity that arises from having multiple sources
    19  of instances is through the use of type synonyms. In this case, we use the type synonym `WithAbs`
    20  of a semiring. In particular this type synonym depends on an absolute value, which provides a
    21  systematic way of assigning and inferring instances of the semiring that also depend on an absolute
    22  value. The completion of a field at multiple absolute values is defined in
    23  `Mathlib/Analysis/Normed/Field/WithAbs.lean` as `AbsoluteValue.Completion`. The completion of a
    24  number field at an infinite place is then derived in this file, as `InfinitePlace` is a subtype of
    25  `AbsoluteValue`.
    26  
    27  ## Main definitions
    28  - `NumberField.InfinitePlace.Completion` : the completion of a number field `K` at an infinite
    29    place, obtained by completing `K` with respect to the absolute value associated to the infinite
    30    place.
    31  - `NumberField.InfinitePlace.Completion.extensionEmbedding` : the embedding `v.embedding : K →+* ℂ`
    32    extended to `v.Completion →+* ℂ`.
    33  - `NumberField.InfinitePlace.Completion.extensionEmbeddingOfIsReal` : if the infinite place `v`
    34    is real, then this extends the embedding `v.embedding_of_isReal : K →+* ℝ` to
    35    `v.Completion →+* ℝ`.
    36  - `NumberField.InfinitePlace.Completion.ringEquivRealOfIsReal` : the ring isomorphism
    37    `v.Completion ≃+* ℝ` when `v` is a real infinite place; the forward direction of this is
    38    `extensionEmbeddingOfIsReal`.
    39  - `NumberField.InfinitePlace.Completion.ringEquivComplexOfIsComplex` : the ring isomorphism
    40    `v.Completion ≃+* ℂ` when `v` is a complex infinite place; the forward direction of this is
    41    `extensionEmbedding`.
    42  
    43  ## Main results
